newsitem.title: USA: General Housewares expects Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: General Housewares expects Q1 loss.

text.p: General Housewares Inc expects a first-quarter loss of $0.15-$0.20 per share but sees about break-even second quarter results, Chief Financial Officer Robert Gray said Friday.

"Lower-than-expected sales, combined with the planned expenditures supporting the company's initiative to improve customer service, will result in a loss greater than the modest loss that had been anticipated," Gray said of the first quarter.
His remarks to analysts in Chicago were made public by General Housewares.

In the year-ago first quarter, the manufacturer and marketer of cutlery, kitchen tools and specialty cookware reported a loss of $2.2 million, or $0.59 per share, which included various charges and operating losses associated with disposition of a division.

Gray said, "While OXO (Division) sales continued to exceed expectations, a slowdown of orders from certain key customers impacted the Chicago Cutlery and Granite Ware lines. This slowdown, coupled with weak performance of the company's outlet store, resulted in the sales shortfall."
He said seasonality of the company's business was exacerbated by the 1996 disposition of the Leyse and Wagner cast iron cookware lines.
"Reflecting the seasonality and current order patterns, we anticipate that our second quarter results will approximate breakeven, which would be in line with the company's 1997 plan," he concluded.
